chunks: Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allah, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from ʿAsim ibn Humayd, who said:
I said to Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام: “May anyone enter the Haram except in a state of ihram?” He said: “No, except one who is ill or suffering from an abdominal ailment.”

key_terms.مَبْطُونٌ: one afflicted with an abdominal illness
key_terms.مُحْرِمًا: in the state of ihram for pilgrimage rites

ai.seo_question: Can someone enter the Haram without being in ihram?
ai.summary: This hadith states the legal ruling that entry into the Haram is not permitted without ihram. It also identifies an exception for a sick person or one afflicted with an abdominal illness, indicating a concession in cases of hardship.
